It asserts the stop is QueueEmpty (not TargetMet), outcome_unchanged == ["a"], that the job line contains "did not change the outcome", and that the display text contains "no landing in this run changed the outcome" and not "target met".

findings.summary: The source check reads only claims.json. The page's intro, transition and glossary text (intro.json) is never compared with the source, so wrong prose on the page can still pass and end the run as "target met".
findings.evidence: study_source collects only `text` from claims.json, and D100 says "Only claims.json statements are checked, not the introduction text." studies/firstmate-work-handling/intro.json repeats the reported wrong facts as page text: line 42 "teardown returns a clean worktree, closes the backlog item and the work is Done", lines 30 and 55 "a place is freed only when a worker records its ready PR or is cleaned up", and line 78 for the teardown glossary entry. The request says the check "must catch statements the source contradicts or leaves out", and the reading says "fail on any statement". If a later job fixes the claims but not the intro, the wrong page passes. This is the same class of fault the request is about, and it was left as a documented tradeoff instead of being fixed.
findings.location: crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs RealSteps::check_page / study_source; docs/decisions.md D100 Tradeoff

findings.summary: The budget check reserves one verifier cap, but check_page makes one capped call per study.
findings.evidence: source_check calls ask() once for each study that has statements, and each call is capped at verifier_usd. With more than one study, spending can go past --budget. Only one study exists today (studies/firstmate-work-handling). D100 acknowledges the cost is "up to the verifier cap per study", but the guard does not match that.

findings.summary: The real source-check path has no test: GitPinner pin, mount, model call and recording.
findings.evidence: pin.rs tests only parse_source_findings. The two real-steps drain tests were changed from TargetMet to QueueEmpty, because their job edits README.md. So no test runs RealSteps::check_page or check_statements_against_source end to end with a fake agent and a stub pinner. D100 says the model call was not run against the live source.

findings.summary: The source-check invocation is recorded as Role::Audience but uses the verifier model and cap.
findings.evidence: agent_spec(..., Role::Audience, &jc.config.models.verifier, ..., jc.config.budget.verifier_usd, ...). The role label in the mirrored invocation may mislead anyone reading the cost breakdown.

summary: I read the full diff and ran the drain tests, the athena-cli tests, fmt, clippy and `athena drain --help`. All of them passed. The first rule works: a landing only counts toward "target met" if its diff touches OUTCOME_PATHS. Other landings still count as landed, but the report names them as "did not change the outcome", and stubbed drains show both the blocked case and the normal case where the target is met. The source check is now a model call that reads the source at the commit in pin.json. It is guarded by the budget (using the verifier cap), its cost is added to spent_usd, and it keeps the old self-consistency check as a free first step. The docs, --help, D100 and CHANGELOG all describe it. The verdict is still fail, because the check only reads `claims.json`. The page also shows text from `intro.json`: the intro, the transition list and the glossary. Those lines repeat the facts that were reported wrong, for example "teardown … closes the backlog item and the work is Done" and "a place is freed only when a worker records its ready PR or is cleaned up". None of them is checked. So a page with wrong prose can still pass and end the run as "target met". D100 records this as a tradeoff instead of fixing it, which falls short of the request's "must catch statements the source contradicts or leaves out". Smaller gaps: the budget check reserves one verifier cap but makes one call per study; the real call path through the pin, mount and model call has no test; and the two real-steps drain tests no longer reach TargetMet.
